verdict: Broadcom closed its first full year with VMware by growing revenue 51% to $14.1B, and a $442M tax benefit lifted net income to $4.3B — capping a record year in which AI chips and VMware remade the company.

kpis.label: Semiconductor revenue
kpis.note: +12% YoY — AI revenue hit $12.2B for fiscal 2024

segments.name: Semiconductor solutions
segments.note: Chips — above all custom AI accelerators and networking gear for data centers. AI semiconductor revenue grew 220% across fiscal 2024 to $12.2B.

segments.name: Infrastructure software
segments.note: VMware and other enterprise software — up 196% YoY with a full quarter of VMware included (the deal had only just closed in the year-ago quarter).

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next chips and software — a smaller share of each revenue dollar than most chip rivals spend.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization & restructuring
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands and technology bought in acquisitions (VMware above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — plus restructuring and other charges.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $916M on Broadcom's debt, plus $52M of other income and $119M of profit from discontinued operations — a net -$745M below operating profit.
footerNote: The tax line was a benefit, not a bill: a $442M income-tax benefit is drawn as a green source into net profit. Net income of $4,324M includes $119M from discontinued operations; continuing operations earned $4,205M.

takeaways.title: VMware transformed the mix
takeaways.text: Infrastructure software revenue nearly tripled to $5.8B with a full quarter of VMware included — Broadcom is now as much a software company as a chip company, with software at 41% of revenue.

takeaways.title: AI carried the chip business
takeaways.text: Semiconductor revenue was a record $30.1B for fiscal 2024, driven by $12.2B of AI revenue — up 220% — from custom AI accelerators (XPUs) and Ethernet networking gear.

takeaways.title: A tax benefit padded profit
takeaways.text: GAAP net income of $4,324M was helped by a $442M income-tax benefit. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, which strips out $2,415M of acquisition amortization and $1,314M of stock pay, net income was $6,965M.

oneTimers: GAAP profit carries $2,415M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets ($1,602M inside cost of revenue and $813M inside operating expenses) — mostly bookkeeping from the VMware deal, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $6,965M instead of $4,324M.
A $442M income-tax benefit — a benefit, not a bill — is drawn as a green 'Tax benefit' source in the chart.
Discontinued operations added $119M below the line — profit from businesses being exited; profit from continuing operations was $4,205M.
